classification.difficultyReason: Eliminate t from the velocity components, solve the quadratic for the landing x (it factorises), then differentiate to get the landing direction. These are routine linked steps with no signposting.

content.prompt:
A ball is thrown from the edge of a $20\text{ m}$ high platform with initial velocity $(20\mathbf{i}+15\mathbf{j})\text{ m/s}$. Use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

Taking the origin at the point of projection, find the Cartesian equation of the path and hence the direction of motion when the ball lands, to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\dot{x}&=20,\qquad\dot{y}=15-10t\\x&=20t,\qquad y=15t-5t^2\\t&=\frac{x}{20}\\y&=15\left(\frac{x}{20}\right)-5\left(\frac{x}{20}\right)^2\\y&=\frac34x-\frac{x^2}{80}\end{aligned}$$
The ground is at $y=-20$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac34x-\frac{x^2}{80}&=-20\\x^2-60x-1600&=0\\(x-80)(x+20)&=0\\x&=80\end{aligned}$$
The direction of motion is given by the gradient:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac34-\frac{x}{40}\\\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=80}&=\frac34-2=-\frac54\\\tan^{-1}\left(\frac54\right)&\approx51^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The gradient is negative, so the direction is $51^\circ$ below the horizontal.
